Fix \((P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n\) and
\(0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0\). By \texttt{ass:positivity},
\[
\{0<e(X)\leq\lambda\}
=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{j=0}^{\infty}
\{2^{-j-1}\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{-j}\lambda\}
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The upper half of \texttt{ass:uniform-shell} and countable additivity give
\[
P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\leq c_+\lambda^\kappa\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}2^{-j\kappa}
={c_+\over1-2^{-\kappa}}\lambda^\kappa.
\]
The shell with upper endpoint \(\lambda\) and the lower half of the same
assumption give
\[
P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\geq P\{\lambda/2<e(X)\leq\lambda\}
\geq c_-\lambda^\kappa.
\]
This proves the first uniform equivalence and states explicitly where positivity
is used.

Put \(H_\lambda=E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]\). The part below \(\lambda\)
satisfies
\[
c_-\lambda^{\kappa-1}
\leq {P\{e(X)\leq\lambda\}\over\lambda}
\leq {c_+\over1-2^{-\kappa}}\lambda^{\kappa-1}.             \tag{1}
\]
Let \(J\) be the largest nonnegative integer for which
\(2^J\lambda\leq\lambda_0\), when such an integer exists. On the shell
\(2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\), inverse propensity is at most
\((2^j\lambda)^{-1}\), and the upper shell bound at
\(2^{j+1}\lambda\) yields
\[
E_P\!\left[
{\mathbf 1\{2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\}\over e(X)}
\right]
\leq2c_+(2^{j+1}\lambda)^{\kappa-1}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The possible terminal piece and \(\{e(X)>\lambda_0\}\) contribute at most a
constant depending only on \((c_+,\kappa,\lambda_0)\). Thus
\[
H_\lambda\leq C\left[1+\lambda^{\kappa-1}
\sum_{j=0}^{J}2^{j(\kappa-1)}\right].                       \tag{3}
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the geometric sum in (3) is bounded, and (1) gives
\(H_\lambda\asymp\lambda^{\kappa-1}\). If \(\kappa=1\), every complete
shell between \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda_0\) contributes at least
\[
{1\over2^{j+1}\lambda}
P\{2^j\lambda<e(X)\leq2^{j+1}\lambda\}\geq {c_-\over2},
\]
while (2) gives a constant upper contribution per shell. The number of shells
is comparable to \(1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)\), and hence
\(H_\lambda\asymp1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)\). If \(\kappa>1\), the sum in
(3) is bounded after its largest term is combined with
\(\lambda^{\kappa-1}\), whereas the fixed top shell gives
\[
H_\lambda\geq\lambda_0^{-1}
P\{\lambda_0/2<e(X)\leq\lambda_0\}
\geq c_-\lambda_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
These cases are exactly
\(H_\lambda\asymp v_\kappa(\lambda)^2\). Every comparison constant is
independent of \(P\), \(n\), and \(\lambda\).

Fix a member \((P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n\). Write
\[
\Delta=g_1-g_0,\qquad h_a=m_a-g_a,\qquad
\varepsilon_a=Y-g_a(X)\ \text{on }\{D=a\},\qquad e_\lambda=e\vee\lambda.
\]
By \texttt{ass:right-overlap}, the range of \(e\) is contained in
\([0,1-\eta_+/2]\). Metric projection onto this interval and the map
\(z\mapsto z\vee\lambda\) are contractions. Therefore
\[
|p^\circ-e|\leq|p-e|,\qquad
|q_\lambda-e_\lambda|\leq|p^\circ-e|\leq|p-e|,
\qquad1-p^\circ\geq\eta_+/2.                              \tag{4}
\]
All divisions below are legitimate because \(\lambda>0\),
\texttt{ass:positivity} gives \(e>0\) almost surely, and
\texttt{ass:right-overlap} gives \(1-e\geq\eta_+>0\).

The target is the given identifying functional
\(\tau(P)=E_P[\Delta(X)]\); consistency and ignorability justify its causal
interpretation, rather than define the statistic. The score has the exact
identity
\[
\psi_\lambda
=\Delta+h_1-h_0+{D(\varepsilon_1-h_1)\over q_\lambda}
-{(1-D)(\varepsilon_0-h_0)\over1-p^\circ}.                \tag{5}
\]
For the sharp first-moment bound, add and subtract the true clipped treated
denominator and the true control denominator. Pointwise,
\[
\begin{split}
\psi_\lambda-\tau(P)
={}&A+B_1+B_0+C_1+C_0+R_1+R_0,\\
A={}&\Delta-\tau(P)+{D\varepsilon_1\over e_\lambda}
-{(1-D)\varepsilon_0\over1-e},\\
B_1={}&h_1\left(1-{D\over e_\lambda}\right),\qquad
B_0=-h_0\left(1-{1-D\over1-e}\right),\\
C_1={}&D\varepsilon_1\left({1\over q_\lambda}-{1\over e_\lambda}\right),\\
C_0={}&-(1-D)\varepsilon_0
\left({1\over1-p^\circ}-{1\over1-e}\right),\\
R_1={}&Dh_1\left({1\over e_\lambda}-{1\over q_\lambda}\right),\qquad
R_0=(1-D)h_0\left({1\over1-p^\circ}-{1\over1-e}\right).
\end{split}                                                   \tag{6}
\]
The definitions of \(g_0\) and \(g_1\) give
\(E_P(\varepsilon_a\mid D=a,X)=0\). Hence
\(E_PA=E_PC_1=E_PC_0=E_PB_0=0\), and
\[
E_PB_1=E_P\!\left[h_1(X)
\left(1-{e(X)\over e_\lambda(X)}\right)\right].
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, \texttt{ass:public-g1-radius}, and
\texttt{lem:uniform-shell-calculus},
\[
|E_PB_1|
\leq r_{1n}P\{e(X)<\lambda\}^{1/2}
\leq C r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}.                         \tag{7}
\]

We next bound centered empirical terms. The signal and conditional residual
variance assumptions give
\[
\|A\|_{P,2}
\leq C\left\{1+E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]^{1/2}\right\}
\leq C v_\kappa(\lambda).                                  \tag{8}
\]
Indeed,
\[
E_P\!\left[{D\varepsilon_1^2\over e_\lambda^2}\right]
\leq\sigma_1^2E_P\!\left[{e\over e_\lambda^2}\right]
\leq\sigma_1^2E_P[e_\lambda^{-1}],
\]
the control residual term is at most \(\sigma_0^2/\eta_+\), and
\(\|\Delta-E_P\Delta\|_{P,2}\leq\|\Delta\|_{P,2}\leq\sqrt M\).
Conditional on \(X\),
\[
E_P\!\left[h_1^2\left(1-{D\over e_\lambda}\right)^2\middle|X\right]
\leq h_1^2(1+\lambda^{-1}),
\]
whereas the control counterpart is at most a fixed multiple of \(h_0^2\).
Consequently,
\[
\|B_1\|_{P,2}\leq r_{1n}\sqrt{1+\lambda^{-1}},
\qquad \|B_0\|_{P,2}\leq C r_{0n}.                       \tag{9}
\]
Using (4), \(e\leq e_\lambda\), the public propensity certificate, and the
two conditional residual variance bounds,
\[
\begin{split}
E_PC_1^2
&\leq\sigma_1^2E_P\!\left[
{e(p-e)^2\over q_\lambda^2e_\lambda^2}\right]
\leq{\sigma_1^2r_{en}^2\over\lambda^3},\\
E_PC_0^2&\leq C\sigma_0^2r_{en}^2.
\end{split}                                                   \tag{10}
\]
The remainders require no unassumed product second moment. Conditioning on
\(X\), then using (4) and Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
\[
E_P|R_1|\leq{E_P(|h_1||p-e|)\over\lambda}
\leq{r_{1n}r_{en}\over\lambda},
\qquad
E_P|R_0|\leq C r_{0n}r_{en}.                              \tag{11}
\]

For an i.i.d. sample and every square-integrable centered \(Z\),
\(E|\mathbb P_nZ|\leq\{E[(\mathbb P_nZ)^2]\}^{1/2}
=\|Z\|_{P,2}/\sqrt n\). Apply this identity to the centered terms in (6),
use \(E|\mathbb P_nR_a|\leq E|R_a|\) for the remainders, and absorb
\(r_{0n}/\sqrt n\) and \(r_{en}/\sqrt n\) into \(Cn^{-1/2}\) because all
radii are at most \(\bar r\). Equations (7)--(11) yield
\[
E_P|\widehat\tau_\lambda-\tau(P)|
\leq C\left\{
{v_\kappa(\lambda)\over\sqrt n}
+{r_{1n}\over\sqrt{n\lambda}}
+{r_{en}\over\sqrt n\,\lambda^{3/2}}
+r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}
+{r_{1n}r_{en}\over\lambda}
+r_{0n}r_{en}\right\}.                                  \tag{12}
\]

We verify the stated threshold. First suppose its fixed cap does not bind and
write \(L_n\) for the maximum in \texttt{def:oracle-threshold}. Since
\(L_n\geq b_{o,n}\),
\[
{r_{1n}\over\sqrt{nL_n}}\leq r_{1n}L_n^{\kappa/2},          \tag{13}
\]
because \(nL_n^{\kappa+1}\geq1\). Since \(L_n\geq b_{e,n}\),
\(r_{en}\leq L_n^{(\kappa+2)/2}\), and therefore
\[
{r_{en}\over\sqrt nL_n^{3/2}}
\leq {L_n^{(\kappa-1)/2}\over\sqrt n}
\leq\begin{cases}
n^{-1/2}L_n^{-(1-\kappa)/2},&0<\kappa<1,\\
n^{-1/2},&\kappa\geq1.
\end{cases}                                               \tag{14}
\]
Also
\[
{r_{1n}r_{en}\over L_n}
\leq r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}.                    \tag{15}
\]
For \(0<\kappa<1\), \(L_n\geq b_{g,n}\) gives
\[
{v_\kappa(L_n)\over\sqrt n}
\leq n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}
\leq Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}).                                  \tag{16}
\]
For \(\kappa=1\), the same inequality inside the logarithm gives
\[
{v_1(L_n)\over\sqrt n}
\leq Cn^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+\log_+(nr_{1n}^2)}
=C Q_1(n,r_{1n}),                                         \tag{17}
\]
and for \(\kappa>1\) this term is \(Cn^{-1/2}\). Finally,
\[
\begin{split}
r_{1n}L_n^{\kappa/2}
\leq C\{&r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]}
+r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}\\
&+\mathbf 1\{\kappa\leq1\}n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}\}.
\end{split}                                                   \tag{18}
\]
The last term is bounded by \(Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})\), including the value
\(n^{-1/2}\) when \(\kappa=1\). Equations (12)--(18) give
\(E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P)|\leq C\rho_n\) when the cap
does not bind.

If the cap binds, \(\lambda_n^\star=\lambda_0\) and at least one active
component is at least \(\lambda_0\). If it is \(b_{o,n}\), then \(n\) is
bounded by a class constant; bounded radii make every term in (12) a fixed
multiple of \(n^{-1/2}\leq\rho_n\). If it is \(b_{e,n}\), then \(r_{en}\)
is bounded below by a positive class constant. Thus the fixed multiples of
\(r_{1n}\) and \(r_{1n}r_{en}\) in (12) are absorbed by
\(r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}\), while all stochastic terms are fixed
multiples of \(n^{-1/2}\). If \(0<\kappa\leq1\) and it is \(b_{g,n}\), then
\(r_{1n}\leq(n\lambda_0)^{-1/2}\); all terms containing \(r_{1n}\) are then
absorbed by the root-\(n\) component of \(Q_\kappa\), using
\(r_{en}\leq\bar r\). The term \(r_{0n}r_{en}\) already occurs in
\(\rho_n\). These cases exhaust cap binding and prove
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|
\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P)|\leq C\rho_n.       \tag{19}
\]
The statistic is a measurable function of the observed sample and supplied
functions and radii, so \texttt{def:estimator-class} gives membership in
\(\mathcal T_n\). Finally, for
\(W=|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P)|\), the elementary inequality
\(E_PW\geq(C\rho_n/\delta)P\{W>C\rho_n/\delta\}\), with the constant in
(19), proves the displayed fixed-probability bound.

If \(n\geq5\), the five nonempty blocks in
\texttt{def:median-estimator} are independent by \texttt{ass:iid}; each block
statistic is measurable in its block and the deterministic public inputs. The
median is a Borel function of five real numbers. If \(1\leq n<5\), the same
definition uses the measurable full-sample clipped statistic. Hence
\texttt{def:estimator-class} gives
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}\in\mathcal T_n\) in both cases.

Now let \(n\geq5\), put
\(Z_j=\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}^{(j)}-\tau(P)\), and write
\(a=K\rho_n\). The premise and
\(E|Z_j|\geq uP\{|Z_j|>u\}\) give
\(P\{|Z_j|>u\}\leq a/u\). If the median error exceeds \(u\), at least three
of the five events \(\{|Z_j|>u\}\) occur. Independence and a union bound over
the \({5\choose3}=10\) triples yield
\[
P\{|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>u\}
\leq\min\{1,10(a/u)^3\}.                                  \tag{20}
\]
For \(W=|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|\), nonnegative integration of
\(W^2=\int_0^W2u\,du\) gives
\[
E_P[W^2]=\int_0^\infty2uP(W>u)\,du
\leq\int_0^a2u\,du+\int_a^\infty20a^3u^{-2}\,du
=21a^2.
\]
Taking square roots proves the asserted factor \(\sqrt{21}\) and, with the
square explicitly inside the expectation, proves exactly the stated
root-mean-squared conclusion.

Write \(L=1-\eta_+\). Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_n\),
\texttt{ass:uniform-shell} at \(u=\lambda_0\), and
\texttt{ass:right-overlap} imply
\[
L>{\lambda_0\over2}.                                      \tag{21}
\]
Indeed, if \(L\leq\lambda_0/2\), the shell
\(\{\lambda_0/2<e(X)\leq\lambda_0\}\) is empty, contrary to its lower bound
\(c_-\lambda_0^\kappa>0\). Positivity and the lower shell bound also imply
that \(\mathcal X\) is infinite: finitely many positive propensity values have
a positive minimum, leaving all sufficiently small shells empty. Every
infinite standard Borel space contains a countably infinite set of distinct
points, and its singletons are measurable. Thus the countable atomic support
specified by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lb}}\) is measurable.

Set \(a=\min\{L,\lambda_0\}\) and \(q_\ell=a2^{-\ell}\). By (21),
\(\lambda_0/2<a\leq\lambda_0\). Put background mass
\(b_0=c_-\lambda_0^\kappa\) at \(q_0\), and for \(\ell\geq1\) put
\[
b_\ell=c_-q_{\ell-1}^\kappa=2^\kappa c_-q_\ell^\kappa.     \tag{22}
\]
For \(0<u<a\), there is a unique \(\ell\geq1\) with
\(q_\ell\leq u<q_{\ell-1}\), and exactly \(q_\ell\) is in \((u/2,u]\).
Hence
\[
c_-u^\kappa<b_\ell\leq2^\kappa c_-u^\kappa.               \tag{23}
\]
At a dyadic endpoint the adjacent-index convention gives the same weak
inequalities. For \(a\leq u\leq\lambda_0\), the point \(q_0=a\) is in the
shell because \(u<2a\), and
\[
c_-u^\kappa\leq b_0=c_-\lambda_0^\kappa
<2^\kappa c_-a^\kappa.                                    \tag{24}
\]
Thus the background supplies every lower shell bound and has upper coefficient
\(2^\kappa c_-\). Its total mass is
\[
B_{\mathrm{bg}}
=c_-\lambda_0^\kappa+{c_-a^\kappa\over1-2^{-\kappa}}
\leq {1-2^{-\kappa}\over4}+{1\over4}< {1\over2},           \tag{25}
\]
by \texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}.

Let \(\Delta_c=c_+-2^\kappa c_-\). The two richness inequalities imply
\(\Delta_c>0\). Fix \(J\geq3\), \(\zeta=7/10\),
\(s_0=\zeta q_J\), \(\gamma=21/40\), and choose \(A\) below the three positive
caps in \texttt{def:lower-bound-handle}. Put
\[
t_j=s_02^{-j},\qquad w_j=A(1-2^{-\kappa})t_j^\kappa.
\]
For each finite \(N\), give every signal point \(x_{j,k}\) and companion
\(\widetilde x_{j,k}\) mass \(w_j/N\). The signal mass and companion mass are
separately
\[
\sum_{j\geq0}w_j
=A(1-2^{-\kappa})s_0^\kappa\sum_{j\geq0}2^{-j\kappa}
=As_0^\kappa.                                            \tag{26}
\]
Reserve their combined mass by \(R_{J+j}=2w_j\). With
\(d_\ell=c_+q_\ell^\kappa-b_\ell-R_\ell\), one has
\(d_\ell\geq0\): this is immediate below level \(J\), including \(\ell=0\)
from the richness bounds, and for \(\ell\geq J\) it follows from
\[
b_\ell+R_\ell
=\{2^\kappa c_-+2A(1-2^{-\kappa})\zeta^\kappa\}q_\ell^\kappa
\leq c_+q_\ell^\kappa.                                    \tag{27}
\]

Let \(S=c_+a^\kappa/(1-2^{-\kappa})\). We claim \(S\geq1\). If
\(a=L\leq\lambda_0\), take a member of the nonempty class. Positivity and
right overlap make the disjoint shells
\(\{q_{\ell+1}<e(X)\leq q_\ell\}\), \(\ell\geq0\), a partition up to null
sets, so their upper shell bounds imply
\[
1\leq\sum_{\ell\geq0}c_+q_\ell^\kappa=S.                 \tag{28}
\]
If \(a=\lambda_0<L\), \texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness} gives
\[
S\geq{2^{\kappa-1}\over1-2^{-\kappa}}\geq1.               \tag{29}
\]
Consequently,
\[
D_{\mathrm{cap}}:=\sum_{\ell\geq0}d_\ell
=S-B_{\mathrm{bg}}-2As_0^\kappa
\geq1-B_{\mathrm{bg}}-2As_0^\kappa=:H>0.                 \tag{30}
\]
Put \(\pi_\ell=Hd_\ell/D_{\mathrm{cap}}\) at a distinct completion point of
propensity \(q_\ell\). Then \(0\leq\pi_\ell\leq d_\ell\),
\(\sum_\ell\pi_\ell=H\), and the exact total-mass identity is
\[
\sum_{\ell\geq0}b_\ell+2\sum_{j\geq0}w_j+
\sum_{\ell\geq0}\pi_\ell
=B_{\mathrm{bg}}+2As_0^\kappa+H=1.                       \tag{31}
\]

For the shell upper bound, first put the active reserved mass back at its
virtual endpoint. Its total endpoint mass is
\[
M_\ell=b_\ell+\pi_\ell+R_\ell\leq c_+q_\ell^\kappa.       \tag{32}
\]
The actual law relocates \(R_\ell\) into \([\gamma q_\ell,q_\ell)\). This
contains unchanged active propensities because \(t_j=\zeta q_{J+j}\), treated
fuzzy ratios in \([4/5,4/3]\), and control fuzzy ratios in \([3/4,5/4]\), since
\[
{4\over5}\zeta>{21\over40},\qquad {4\over3}\zeta<1,
\qquad {3\over4}\zeta={21\over40},\qquad {5\over4}\zeta<1. \tag{33}
\]
The signal point receives one tilt and its companion the opposite tilt, so the
unordered pair of relocated propensities is independent of the fixed sign and
of \(\theta\).

Fix \(0<u<a\) and the unique \(\ell\geq1\) with
\(q_\ell\leq u<q_{\ell-1}\). Relocation from \(q_\ell\) adds no more than
the mass removed there; all lower endpoints remain at or below \(u/2\). Only
relocation from \(q_{\ell-1}\) can add further mass, and only when
\(u\geq2\gamma q_\ell\). Thus
\[
P\{u/2<e(X)\leq u\}
\leq M_\ell+R_{\ell-1}\mathbf 1\{u\geq2\gamma q_\ell\}.   \tag{34}
\]
When the indicator is one, the third cap on \(A\) gives
\[
R_{\ell-1}
\leq2^{\kappa+1}A(1-2^{-\kappa})\zeta^\kappa q_\ell^\kappa
\leq c_+\{(2\gamma)^\kappa-1\}q_\ell^\kappa
\leq c_+(u^\kappa-q_\ell^\kappa).                         \tag{35}
\]
Equations (32)--(35) prove the upper cap. When \(a\leq u\leq\lambda_0\),
all active propensities are below \(q_J<a/2\), and the endpoint capacity at
\(q_0=a\) gives the same cap. Because background atoms are never relocated,
(23)--(24) give the lower cap for every fixed-sign law. Hence
\[
c_-u^\kappa\leq P\{u/2<e(X)\leq u\}\leq c_+u^\kappa,
\qquad0<u\leq\lambda_0.                                  \tag{36}
\]

We now isolate the signal reservoir
\(S_N=\bigcup_{j\geq0}\{x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\}\); the companion reservoir
is \(C_N=\bigcup_{j\geq0}\{\widetilde x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\}\).
For \(0<v\leq s_0\), let \(j(v)=\min\{j:t_j\leq v\}\). Then
\(v/2<t_{j(v)}\leq v\), and exact geometric summation gives
\[
P_X(S_N\cap\{e_0\leq v\})
=\sum_{j\geq j(v)}w_j=A t_{j(v)}^\kappa,
\qquad A2^{-\kappa}v^\kappa<P_X(S_N\cap\{e_0\leq v\})\leq Av^\kappa, \tag{37}
\]
and
\[
E_P[e_0\mathbf 1\{X\in S_N,e_0\leq v\}]
={A(1-2^{-\kappa})\over1-2^{-(\kappa+1)}}
t_{j(v)}^{\kappa+1}\asymp v^{\kappa+1}.                    \tag{38}
\]
For every \(0<s\leq s_0/2\), the half-open interval \((s,2s]\) contains
exactly one active dyadic level. If \(s=t_j\), that level is
\(t_{j-1}=2s\); otherwise the unique \(j\) with
\(t_j<2s<t_{j-1}\) has \(t_j\in(s,2s)\). Therefore
\[
B_s^S:=S_N\cap\{s<e_0\leq2s\}=\{x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\},
\qquad m:=P_X(B_s^S)=w_j\asymp s^\kappa,                    \tag{39}
\]
and its separately defined companion set
\(C_s^S=\{\widetilde x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\}\) also has mass \(m\).
In particular, for fixed \(j_c\geq1\) and \(s_c=t_{j_c+1}\),
\[
B_c^S:=S_N\cap\{s_c<e_0\leq2s_c\}
=\{x_{j_c,k}:1\leq k\leq N\},\qquad
m_*:=P_X(B_c^S)=w_{j_c}>0.                              \tag{40}
\]
The companion set \(C_c^S\) has the same mass. Background and completion
atoms, including those at \(q_{J+j_c+1}\) in the numerical band in (40), are
outside \(S_N\), remain unperturbed, and are absent from (37)--(40).

We use the following elementary testing reduction. If sample laws \(Q_+\) and
\(Q_-\) have targets separated by at least \(2d\), the two events of estimation
within \(d\) of the respective targets are disjoint. The variational
definition of total variation gives
\[
Q_+\{|T-\tau_+|\geq d\}+Q_-\{|T-\tau_-|\geq d\}
\geq1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_+,Q_-).                         \tag{41}
\]
For prior mixtures, if their sample total variation is at most \(\Gamma\), and
each prior target is within \(d/4\) of centers separated by \(2d\) except with
prior probability \(\varepsilon\), testing the nearer center gives error at
least \((1-\Gamma-2\varepsilon)/2\) for one mixture. Since mixture
probability is an average of fixed-law probabilities, a fixed law in its
support inherits the bound.

For every family, generate \(D\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e(X))\),
generate \((Y_0,Y_1)\) conditionally independently of \(D\) given \(X\), set
\(Y=DY_1+(1-D)Y_0\), and take \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) independently. This verifies
\texttt{ass:ignorability}, \texttt{ass:consistency}, and \texttt{ass:iid}.
For Gaussian treated mean-shift families use centered treated residual noise
with a fixed variance \(0<\sigma^2\leq\sigma_1^2\); use zero residual noise in
all other arms and families. Choose a fixed \(c_A>0\), depending only on class
constants, so small that \(c_A\bar r\leq\sqrt M/4\), every displayed nuisance
radius inequality below holds, and \(c_A\leq\min\{1/4,s_c\}\). Every
treatment-effect signal then has squared \(L^2(P_X)\) norm at most \(M\), and
the two residual-variance assumptions hold. No separate moment bound on
\(g_0\), \(g_1\), or \(Y\) is used. Equations (32)--(36) give positivity and
the shell law; (33) and \(q_J<L\) give right overlap.

For the parametric obstruction, split the top background mass \(b_0\) between
two distinct points of the same propensity. Give them fixed treatment effects
\(+c_A\) and \(-c_A\), set public nuisances equal to the true nuisances, and
under \(\theta\in\{-1,1\}\) assign their masses
\(b_0/2+\theta\epsilon_n\) and \(b_0/2-\theta\epsilon_n\), where
\(\epsilon_n=c_pn^{-1/2}\) and \(0<c_p<b_0/4\). All propensity shells are
unchanged. The one-observation categorical divergence is
\[
2\epsilon_n\log{b_0/2+\epsilon_n\over b_0/2-\epsilon_n}
\leq{16\epsilon_n^2\over b_0},                            \tag{42}
\]
so product divergence is at most \(16c_p^2/b_0\). If \(f=dQ_+/dQ_-\), the
pointwise inequality \(f\log f-f+1\geq(\sqrt f-1)^2\), integration, and
Cauchy--Schwarz give
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_+,Q_-)^2\leq\operatorname{KL}(Q_+,Q_-)\).
Decreasing \(c_p\) makes product total variation at most \(1/4\). The targets
differ by \(4c_Ac_pn^{-1/2}\), so (41) proves the root-\(n\) obstruction.

For \(0<\kappa<1\) and \(r_{1n}>0\), first suppose
\(s=(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\leq s_0\). On the signal-only tail
\(A_s^S=S_N\cap\{e_0\leq s\}\), put \(m_s=P_X(A_s^S)\asymp s^\kappa\) and
\[
m_1=0,\qquad p=e_0,\qquad
g_{1,\pm}=\pm h\mathbf 1_{A_s^S},\qquad
h={c_A r_{1n}\over\sqrt{m_s}},\qquad g_0=m_0=0.             \tag{43}
\]
Then \(\|m_1-g_{1,\pm}\|_2=c_A r_{1n}\leq r_{1n}\) and the signal moment is
\(c_A^2r_{1n}^2\leq M\). By (38),
\(E[e_0\mathbf 1_{A_s^S}]\leq Csm_s\), and direct Gaussian integration gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
={2nh^2\over\sigma^2}E[e_0\mathbf 1_{A_s^S}]
\leq Cc_A^2,                                               \tag{44}
\]
whereas
\[
|\tau(P_+)-\tau(P_-)|=2hm_s
\asymp n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}.                    \tag{45}
\]
If \(s>s_0\), this scale is a class-constant multiple of at most
\(n^{-1/2}\), already covered by (42). If \(r_{1n}=0\), only the parametric
part of \(Q_\kappa\) remains.

At \(\kappa=1\), first assume \(r_{1n}>0\) and set
\(s=(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\). If \(s\leq s_0\), define
\[
J_s=\max\{j:t_j\geq s\},\qquad K_s=J_s+1,\qquad
a_s={c_A\over\sqrt{nK_s}},\qquad
f={a_s\over e_0}\mathbf 1\{X\in S_N,\ s\leq e_0\leq s_0\}. \tag{46}
\]
Here \(w_j=(A/2)t_j\). Exact finite sums give
\[
\|f\|_2^2={Aa_s^2(2^{K_s}-1)\over2s_0}\asymp{a_s^2\over s},
\qquad E[e_0f^2]={A\over2}a_s^2K_s,
\qquad E[f]={A\over2}a_sK_s.                               \tag{47}
\]
Because \(s_02^{-J_s}\geq s>s_02^{-(J_s+1)}\), the first comparison is exact
up to fixed constants. With \(g_{1,\pm}=\pm f\), (47) and
\(s^{-1}=nr_{1n}^2\) imply \(\|f\|_2\leq r_{1n}\) after calibrating \(c_A\),
and
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
={2n\over\sigma^2}E[e_0f^2]\leq Cc_A^2,
\qquad
2E[f]\asymp n^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+\log_+(nr_{1n}^2)}.            \tag{48}
\]
If \(s>s_0\), the logarithm is bounded and (42) applies. If \(r_{1n}=0\),
we do not define \(s\) and again use (42). When \(\kappa>1\),
\(Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})=n^{-1/2}\). This proves the full \(Q_\kappa\) channel.

For the empty-treated-shell channel, choose a fixed small \(c_s\leq s_0\) and
put \(s=c_sn^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\). Use (43) on
\(A_s^S=S_N\cap\{e_0\leq s\}\). Couple the two samples identically unless an
observation lies in \(A_s^S\) and is treated. Equations (37)--(38) and a union
bound give
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
\leq nP\{X\in A_s^S,D=1\}
\leq Cns^{\kappa+1}=Cc_s^{\kappa+1}.                       \tag{49}
\]
Choose \(c_s\) so this is at most \(1/4\). Because the regression norm uses
only the signal mass \(m_s\), target separation is
\[
2hm_s\asymp r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]}.               \tag{50}
\]
The component is zero when \(r_{1n}=0\).

For the treated nuisance product, suppose \(r_{en}>0\). Choose a fixed
\(c_s>0\), depending only on \(\bar r\) and class constants, so that
\[
s=c_sr_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\leq s_0/2                      \tag{51}
\]
and the radius inequality below holds. Equation (39) supplies a unique signal
level \(B_s^S\) of signal mass \(m\asymp s^\kappa\), together with a separate
companion set of mass \(m\). Let \(\delta=1/4\), draw independent signs with
\[
\Pr_\theta(Z_k=z)={1+\theta\delta z\over2},                 \tag{52}
\]
put \(g_1=hZ_k\), \(h=c_A r_{1n}/\sqrt m\), only on the signal cells, and put
all regressions equal to zero on companions. On a signal--companion pair set
\[
e^S_{\theta,Z}={e_0\over1+\theta\delta Z_k},\qquad
e^C_{\theta,Z}={e_0\over1-\theta\delta Z_k},\qquad p=e_0.   \tag{53}
\]
The regression error and signal moment use the signal mass only:
\[
\|m_1-g_1\|_2=h\sqrt m=c_A r_{1n}\leq r_{1n},
\qquad E[(g_1-g_0)^2]=h^2m=c_A^2r_{1n}^2\leq M.             \tag{54}
\]
Each propensity error is at most \(e_0/3\leq2s/3\), but its norm uses the
combined pair mass \(2m\). Hence
\[
\|p-e_{\theta,Z}\|_2
\leq {2s\over3}\sqrt{2m}
\leq Cc_s^{(\kappa+2)/2}r_{en}\leq r_{en}.                 \tag{55}
\]
The propensity ratios lie in \([4/5,4/3]\), so (33)--(36) verify positivity,
right overlap, and every shell for each fixed sign.

On a signal row, including its treated outcome with mean \(hz\),
\[
\Pr_\theta(Z_k=z)e^S_{\theta,z}
={1+\theta\delta z\over2}{e_0\over1+\theta\delta z}
={e_0\over2};                                             \tag{56}
\]
the two untreated weights sum to \(1-e_0\). On a companion, the distribution
of \(\theta\delta Z_k\) under (52) is independent of \(\theta\), so its entire
one-row mixture is independent of \(\theta\). Thus sample mixtures differ only
if two observations hit the same pair index. Since pair index \(k\) has
combined mass \(2m/N\),
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\overline P_+^n,\overline P_-^n)
\leq{2n(n-1)m^2\over N}.                                  \tag{57}
\]
Only signal cells contribute to the target:
\[
\tau(P_{\theta,Z})={hm\over N}\sum_{k=1}^NZ_k,\qquad
E_\theta\tau=\theta\delta hm,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\theta(\tau)\leq{h^2m^2\over N}.       \tag{58}
\]
Choose finite \(N\) larger than fixed multiples of \(n^2\) and
\(\delta^{-2}\). Then (57) and the elementary second-moment bound for a
\(\delta hm/4\) target deviation are each at most \(1/16\). The prior testing
reduction yields an obstruction of order
\[
hm\asymp r_{1n}s^{\kappa/2}
\asymp r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}.                   \tag{59}
\]
If \(r_{en}=0\) or \(r_{1n}=0\), this component is zero.

For the control product use the fixed signal band \(B_c^S\), its separately
defined companion set \(C_c^S\), and write \(e_0=t_{j_c}=2s_c\). Put
\[
g_0=h_0Z_k,\qquad h_0={c_A r_{0n}\over\sqrt{m_*}},\qquad m_0=0,
\qquad
\xi=c_A\min\left\{{r_{en}\over\sqrt{m_*}},{1\over4}\right\}           \tag{60}
\]
only on signal cells, and set all regressions to zero on companions. Draw
\(Z_k\) with \(\Pr_\theta(Z_k=z)=(1+\theta\xi z)/2\). With
\(a_{\theta,k}=\theta\xi Z_k\), set
\[
e^S_{\theta,Z}={e_0+a_{\theta,k}\over1+a_{\theta,k}},\qquad
e^C_{\theta,Z}={e_0-a_{\theta,k}\over1-a_{\theta,k}},\qquad p=e_0.       \tag{61}
\]
Because \(c_A\leq s_c\), \(|a_{\theta,k}|\leq s_c/4=e_0/8\). Direct
algebra shows
\[
{e^S_{\theta,Z}\over e_0}
=1+{a_{\theta,k}(1-e_0)\over e_0(1+a_{\theta,k})},          \tag{62}
\]
and the companion has the opposite sign. Both ratios lie in
\([3/4,5/4]\), so fixed-sign support and shells follow from (33)--(36). The
regression norm and signal moment use \(m_*\), while the propensity norm uses
the combined pair mass \(2m_*\):
\[
\|m_0-g_0\|_2=h_0\sqrt{m_*}=c_A r_{0n}\leq r_{0n},
\qquad E[(g_1-g_0)^2]=h_0^2m_*=c_A^2r_{0n}^2\leq M,          \tag{63}
\]
and
\[
\|p-e_{\theta,Z}\|_2
\leq{\xi\sqrt{2m_*}\over1-\xi}\leq r_{en}.               \tag{64}
\]
For (64), use the first branch of (60) when
\(r_{en}\leq\sqrt{m_*}/4\), and in the other branch use
\(r_{en}>\sqrt{m_*}/4\), decreasing \(c_A\) once for both.

The signal control row cancels exactly:
\[
\Pr_\theta(Z_k=z)(1-e^S_{\theta,z})
={1+\theta\xi z\over2}{1-e_0\over1+\theta\xi z}
={1-e_0\over2}.                                           \tag{65}
\]
This includes its outcome \(h_0z\); the summed treated row has probability
\(e_0\) and outcome zero. The companion mixture is independent of \(\theta\)
because the distribution of \(\theta\xi Z_k\) is. The collision bound uses
combined pair mass and equals \(2n(n-1)m_*^2/N\). Only signal cells contribute
to the target:
\[
\tau(P_{\theta,Z})=-{h_0m_*\over N}\sum_{k=1}^NZ_k,\qquad
E_\theta\tau=-\theta\xi h_0m_*,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\theta(\tau)\leq{h_0^2m_*^2\over N}.    \tag{66}
\]
Taking \(N\) larger than fixed multiples of \(n^2\) and \(\xi^{-2}\) when
\(\xi>0\), the fuzzy reduction yields half-separation
\[
d_0=\xi h_0m_*
=c_A^2r_{0n}\min\{r_{en},\sqrt{m_*}/4\}.                  \tag{67}
\]
In the first branch this is \(c_A^2r_{0n}r_{en}\). In the second,
\(r_{en}>\sqrt{m_*}/4\) and \(r_{en}\leq\bar r\), so
\[
d_0={c_A^2\sqrt{m_*}\over4}r_{0n}
\geq{c_A^2\sqrt{m_*}\over4\bar r}r_{0n}r_{en}.            \tag{68}
\]
If \(\xi=0\), the desired component is zero.

We have constructed fixed laws in \(\mathcal M_n\), with identical public
functions within each subexperiment, yielding constant testing error at
\[
Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}),\qquad
r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]},\qquad
r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)},\qquad r_{0n}r_{en}.       \tag{69}
\]
All regression and target moments in this list were calibrated from the signal
mass only; propensity errors and collision probabilities used the combined
signal--companion mass. The maximum of the four nonnegative quantities is at
least one quarter of their sum \(\rho_n\). Decreasing a class-constant
separation and taking the minimum of the positive testing probabilities gives
constants \(c>0\) and \(\delta_0\in(0,1/4)\), independent of \(n\) and the
admissible radii, such that every \(T\in\mathcal T_n\) obeys
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}
P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}\geq\delta_0.                 \tag{70}
\]
For each law, the event in (70) contributes at least \(c\rho_n\) to
absolute loss and at least \(c^2\rho_n^2\) to squared loss. Hence, for every
\(T\in\mathcal T_n\),
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|T-\tau(P)|
\geq c\rho_n\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}
\geq c\delta_0\rho_n,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P\!\left[(T-\tau(P))^2\right]
\geq c^2\rho_n^2\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}
\geq c^2\delta_0\rho_n^2.
\]
Taking the infima in \texttt{def:absolute-risk} and the corrected
\texttt{def:root-mse-risk}, and then taking the square root in the latter,
gives
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\geq c\delta_0\rho_n,
\qquad
\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\geq c\sqrt{\delta_0}\rho_n.
\]
This proves the deviation and both loss lower bounds, complete probability
normalization, and fixed-sign membership without a global observed-outcome
moment assumption.

The upper and lower bounds use the same law--function class \(\mathcal M_n\)
and decision class \(\mathcal T_n\). By
\texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and \texttt{def:absolute-risk},
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}
\leq\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|
\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P)|
\leq C\rho_n.                                             \tag{71}
\]

For \(n\geq5\), every block size \(m_j\) in
\texttt{def:median-estimator} satisfies \(n/9\leq m_j\leq n\). Apply the
finite-sample inequality (12) from \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} on a
block at the common full-sample threshold \(\lambda_n^\star\). Deterministic
bias terms are unchanged, and
\[
m_j^{-1/2}\leq3n^{-1/2},\qquad
m_j^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\leq9^{1/(\kappa+1)}n^{-1/(\kappa+1)},\qquad
(m_jr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\leq9(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}.                  \tag{72}
\]
Thus the substitutions (13)--(18), with only fixed numerical changes, give
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|
\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}^{(j)}-\tau(P)|\leq K\rho_n. \tag{73}
\]
Block independence follows from \texttt{ass:iid}. Therefore
\texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade} gives
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}
\left\{E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P))^2\right]\right\}^{1/2}
\leq\sqrt{21}\,K\rho_n.                                  \tag{74}
\]

It remains to check \(1\leq n<5\) without bounding \(g_0\), \(g_1\), or
\(Y\) separately. In this range
\[
\lambda_n^\star\geq
\lambda_{\min}:=\min\{\lambda_0,4^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\}>0,
\qquad1-p^\circ\geq\eta_+/2.                              \tag{75}
\]
Use the exact identity (5) with
\(\Delta=g_1-g_0\), \(h_a=m_a-g_a\), and the arm-specific residuals. The
triangle inequality, the signal moment, the public regression certificates,
and the conditional residual variances imply
\[
\begin{split}
\|\psi_{\lambda_n^\star}\|_{P,2}
\leq{}&\sqrt M+r_{1n}+r_{0n}
+\lambda_{\min}^{-1}\sqrt{2(\sigma_1^2+r_{1n}^2)}\\
&+{2\over\eta_+}\sqrt{2(\sigma_0^2+r_{0n}^2)}
\leq C_0.
\end{split}                                                   \tag{76}
\]
For example,
\[
E_P\!\left[{D(\varepsilon_1-h_1)^2\over q_{\lambda_n^\star}^2}\right]
\leq {2(\sigma_1^2+r_{1n}^2)\over\lambda_{\min}^2},
\]
and the analogous control expression is at most
\(8(\sigma_0^2+r_{0n}^2)/\eta_+^2\). Also
\(|\tau(P)|\leq\|\Delta\|_{P,2}\leq\sqrt M\). Convexity of the square gives
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\leq {1\over n}\sum_{i=1}^n
E_P\!\left[(\psi_{\lambda_n^\star}(O_i)-\tau(P))^2\right]
\leq C_1^2.                                               \tag{77}
\]
Since \(\rho_n\geq n^{-1/2}\geq1/2\), (77) is at most
\((2C_1\rho_n)^2\). This proves the root-MSE upper bound for the full-sample
fallback using only \(M\), \(\bar r\), \(\sigma_0^2\), \(\sigma_1^2\),
\(\lambda_{\min}\), and \(\eta_+\). The median rule belongs to
\(\mathcal T_n\), so the corrected \texttt{def:root-mse-risk} gives
\(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\leq C\rho_n\) for every \(n\).

For fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\), the deviation conclusion of
\texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and \texttt{def:probability-risk} give
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}\leq C_\delta\rho_n. \tag{78}
\]
Conversely, \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} gives both loss lower bounds and
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}\geq\delta_0
\quad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal T_n.                   \tag{79}
\]
If \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\) and \(u<c\rho_n\), then
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|>u\}
\geq\delta_0\geq\delta.                                  \tag{80}
\]
Taking the two infima in \texttt{def:probability-risk} proves its lower bound.
Equations (71)--(80) and the two loss lower bounds prove all three uniform
equivalences. The converse uses the reservoir-rich shell class; the upper
bounds used only the broader uniform-shell conditions.

For \(n\geq5\), equation (73) verifies the premise of
\texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade} uniformly, hence
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>u\}
\leq\min\{1,10(K\rho_n/u)^3\}.                            \tag{81}
\]
For \(1\leq n<5\), \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and
\(E|Z|\geq tP\{|Z|>t\}\) give
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>C\rho_n/\alpha\}
\leq\alpha.                                               \tag{82}
\]
Choose \(K_\alpha\) at least \(K(10/\alpha)^{1/3}\) and at least the
finite-sample multiplier in (82). Then
\[
\inf_{\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
\geq1-\alpha,\qquad
\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})=2K_\alpha\rho_n. \tag{83}
\]
The center is measurable in \(O^{(n)}\), and its deterministic radius uses only
the supplied constants and certified radii. Thus
\(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\), proving the honest expected-length
upper bound.

For the converse, take a two-point subexperiment from
\texttt{thm:four-channel-converse}, with targets separated by \(2d\) and sample
total variation at most \(\Gamma\). Honesty at both fixed laws, transfer of an
event by the variational definition of total variation, and a union bound imply
under one law
\[
P\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq2d\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma.                                     \tag{84}
\]
Indeed, on the intersection of the two transferred coverage events the
interval contains both targets.

For a fuzzy subexperiment, suppose its prior target is within \(d/4\) of
\(\mu_\theta\) except with prior probability \(\varepsilon\), the centers are
separated by \(2d\), and mixture total variation is at most \(\Gamma\).
Fixed-law honesty averaged under each prior says that the interval intersects
the corresponding \(d/4\)-neighborhood with probability at least
\(1-\alpha-\varepsilon\). Transfer one event between mixtures and intersect
the two events. An interval meeting both neighborhoods has length at least
\(3d/2\), so
\[
\overline P\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq3d/2\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma-2\varepsilon.                        \tag{85}
\]
The two-point amplitudes can be chosen with \(\Gamma\leq1/4\); in each fuzzy
family, \(N\) can be enlarged until \(\Gamma+2\varepsilon\leq1/4\), without
changing membership or separation. Since \(\alpha<1/4\), (84)--(85) have a
positive \(\alpha\)-dependent lower bound. A mixture expectation averages
fixed-sign laws, every one of which lies in \(\mathcal M_n\), so some fixed law
has expected interval length at least a positive constant times \(d\).

Choose the largest component separation in (69). Their sum is at most four
times their maximum, so \(d\geq c\rho_n\) after rescaling. Every uniformly
honest \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\) therefore satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_n)]
\geq c_\alpha\rho_n.                                      \tag{86}
\]
Taking the infimum in \texttt{def:bias-aware-interval} and combining (83) with
(86) proves \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\). The lower bound has the
same reservoir-rich scope as the converse, while the interval upper bound uses
only the broader uniform-shell class.

\]

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Choose \(L=1-\eta_+\), \(a=\min\{L,\lambda_0\}\),
\(q_\ell=a2^{-\ell}\), \(\ell\geq0\), an integer \(J\geq3\),
\(\zeta=7/10\), \(\gamma=21/40\), and \(s_0=\zeta q_J\). Put
background mass \(b_0=c_-\lambda_0^\kappa\) at propensity \(q_0\) and,
for \(\ell\geq1\), mass \(b_\ell=c_-q_{\ell-1}^\kappa\) at propensity
\(q_\ell\). Let \(B_{\mathrm{bg}}=\sum_{\ell\geq0}b_\ell\). Choose
\[
0<A<\min\left\{
{c_+-2^\kappa c_-\over2^{\kappa+1}},
{1-B_{\mathrm{bg}}\over2s_0^\kappa},
{c_+\{(2\gamma)^\kappa-1\}
 \over2^{\kappa+1}(1-2^{-\kappa})\zeta^\kappa}
\right\},
\]
and set
\[
t_j=s_02^{-j},\qquad
w_j=A(1-2^{-\kappa})t_j^\kappa,\qquad j\geq0.
\]
For every finite \(N\), use mutually distinct signal points \(x_{j,k}\),
balancing companions \(\widetilde x_{j,k}\), background points, and completion
points, where \(j\geq0\) and \(1\leq k\leq N\). Give each signal point and
its companion mass \(w_j/N\), and give both public baseline propensity
\(e_0=t_j\). Define the two reservoirs
\[
S_N=\bigcup_{j\geq0}\{x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\},\qquad
C_N=\bigcup_{j\geq0}\{\widetilde x_{j,k}:1\leq k\leq N\}.
\]
Reserve their combined mass \(R_{J+j}=2w_j\) from the virtual endpoint
\(q_{J+j}\), and put \(R_\ell=0\) otherwise. Define
\[
d_\ell=c_+q_\ell^\kappa-b_\ell-R_\ell,\qquad
H=1-B_{\mathrm{bg}}-2As_0^\kappa,\qquad
D_{\mathrm{cap}}=\sum_{\ell\geq0}d_\ell,\qquad
\pi_\ell={H\over D_{\mathrm{cap}}}d_\ell,
\]
and put completion mass \(\pi_\ell\) at its distinct point of propensity
\(q_\ell\). In unchanged families both members of every active pair have
propensity \(t_j\). In a treated fuzzy cell, with
\(a_{\theta,k}=\theta\delta Z_k\), use propensities

prose_updates.tldr: Global prediction accuracy alone does not determine attainable precision for the full-population ATE when treated observations become polynomially rare. Under reservoir-rich uniform one-sided propensity shells satisfying both \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\), the public-function experiment has the matched four-channel minimax rate \(\rho_n\) for absolute risk, genuine root-MSE, fixed-probability error, and honest expected length. Only the clipped achievability and corresponding risk and interval upper bounds extend to the broader uniform-shell class without those richness restrictions. The proof uses a complete atomic law with signal-only localization, while the upper score and finite-sample fallback require only the treatment-effect signal, public approximation radii, and arm-specific residual variances. Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.

Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than this matched four-risk frontier. The accepted-bank result \(\texttt{stat\_policy\_regret\_margin\_overlap\_v1}\) studies margin-localized policy-welfare regret under coupled Tsybakov margin and one-sided-overlap decay with conditional ERM achievability assumptions. Neither accepted target or class subsumes this binary-treatment full-population ATE experiment under public global \(L^2\) certificates, and this experiment does not subsume either accepted result.
project_justification.niche: The model isolates the statistical price of knowing only global prediction-error guarantees when the treated design vanishes at a boundary. Three treated-side obstructions coexist with the regular control-side product. The primitive moment conditions are a treatment-effect signal bound and arm-specific conditional residual-variance bounds; no separate global second moment of the observed outcome or either regression is imposed.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives explicit decision classes, clipped and median estimators, a bias-aware interval, and a law-by-law four-channel converse. The converse defines a signal reservoir \(S_N\), a disjoint companion reservoir \(C_N\), dyadic background and completion atoms, and signal-only bands \(A_s^S\), \(B_s^S\), and \(B_c^S\). Regression norms and target separation use signal mass, whereas propensity errors and collision bounds use combined pair mass. Endpoint atoms in the same numerical bands stay unperturbed, and the explicit completion capacities retain the exact total-mass and fixed-sign shell proofs.

Fix \(\kappa>0\).  Suppose for contradiction that
\((P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), and set
\[
u_\star=\frac12\min\{\lambda_0,\eta_-\}.
\]
The declared ranges \(\lambda_0\in(0,1)\) and \(\eta_-\in(0,1)\) imply
\(0<u_\star\leq\lambda_0\) and \(u_\star<\eta_-\).  Membership in
\(\mathcal M_n\), by \texttt{def:public-weak-overlap-class}, entails
\texttt{ass:uniform-shell}.  Therefore
\[
P\!\left\{\frac{u_\star}{2}<e(X)\leq u_\star\right\}
\geq c_-u_\star^\kappa>0,                                                \tag{1}
\]
where the strict inequality follows from \(c_->0\), \(u_\star>0\), and
\(\kappa>0\).  On the other hand, membership in
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), by \texttt{def:regular-overlap-class},
entails \texttt{ass:uniform-overlap-comparator}, and hence
\[
P\{e(X)\geq\eta_-\}=1.                                                   \tag{2}
\]
Since
\[
\left\{\frac{u_\star}{2}<e(X)\leq u_\star\right\}
\subseteq\{e(X)<\eta_-\},
\]
equation (2) says that the probability in (1) is zero, a contradiction.
Thus
\[
\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\varnothing.                \tag{3}
\]

Next fix \(n\in\mathbb N\) and
\((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\).  Thus \(n\geq1\) and all
three radii are nonnegative.  For every \(\kappa>1\),
\texttt{def:tail-noise-rate} gives
\[
Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})=n^{-1/2}.                                             \tag{4}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{\kappa}{2(\kappa+1)}\longrightarrow\frac12,
\qquad
\frac{\kappa}{\kappa+2}\longrightarrow1.                               \tag{5}
\]
Because \(n\geq1\), continuity of the exponential map in the exponent
implies
\[
r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]}
\longrightarrow r_{1n}n^{-1/2}.                                         \tag{6}
\]
If \(r_{en}>0\), continuity likewise gives
\(r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}\to r_{en}\).  If \(r_{en}=0\), both sides
are zero for every positive exponent.  Hence, in all cases,
\[
r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}
\longrightarrow r_{1n}r_{en}.                                           \tag{7}
\]
Substituting (4), (6), and (7) into \texttt{def:sharp-rate}, and passing to
the limit in its finite sum, yields
\[
\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\rho_n
=(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}.                            \tag{8}
\]

Put
\[
A_n=r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\geq0,
\qquad
B_n=n^{-1/2}+A_n>0.
\]
Since \(0\leq r_{1n}\leq\bar r\) and \(\bar r\geq1\),
\[
B_n
\leq(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+A_n
\leq(1+\bar r)n^{-1/2}+A_n
\leq(1+\bar r)B_n.                                                       \tag{9}
\]
The constants in (9) depend only on the fixed cap \(\bar r\), not on
\(n\) or the radius triple.  Thus the expression on the right-hand side of
(8) is uniformly comparable to
\[
n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}.                                     \tag{10}
\]

It remains to verify the two deliberately limited source comparisons.  Define
\[
C_n=n^{-1/2}+r_{0n}r_{en}+r_{1n}r_{en}.
\]
By \texttt{lem:jin-syrgkanis-regular-benchmark}, after the stated
constant-weight interpretive substitutions, the square-root lower-bound form
is
\[
J_n=n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}.
\]
Nonnegativity of the radii gives
\[
\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}
\leq(r_{0n}+r_{1n})r_{en}
\leq2\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
J_n\leq C_n\leq2J_n.                                                     \tag{11}
\]

By \texttt{lem:bonvini-et-al-regular-benchmark}, the Bonvini--Kennedy--Dukes--
Balakrishnan source supplies only the lower-rate template for one mean
functional.  Under only the stated treated-side interpretive substitution
\(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\) and \(\delta_n=r_{en}\), that template is
\[
L_{1,n}=n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}.
\]
Again by nonnegativity,
\[
L_{1,n}\leq C_n.                                                         \tag{12}
\]
No control-side expression or sum of two armwise risks has been inferred in
(12).  The cited leaves concern their own source classes and risk conventions;
neither asserts a matching upper bound, a joint two-arm minimax theorem for
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), or a class inclusion.  Combining (3),
(8)--(12) proves exactly the class separation, fast-tail limit, and algebraic
sanity comparisons in the proposition.

Let \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(w\) be a fixed weight, and let \(e_n,e_n',f_n\ge0\) denote the source paper's squared nuisance-radius parameters.  In the estimator-bounded WATE class \(\mathcal G_{e_n,e_n',f_n}\) of JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 states that the squared \(\gamma\)-quantile minimax risk satisfies
\[
\mathfrak M_{n,\gamma}^{\mathrm{WATE}}(\mathcal G_{e_n,e_n',f_n})
=\Omega\!\left(
\max\{e_n,e_n'\}f_n\lVert w\rVert_{P_X,\infty}^{2}
+\frac{\lVert w\rVert_{P_X,2}^{2}}{n}
\right),
\]
where \(P_X\) is the source class's covariate law.  For \(w\equiv1\), the purely interpretive substitutions \(e_n=r_{0n}^{2}\), \(e_n'=r_{1n}^{2}\), and \(f_n=r_{en}^{2}\) turn the square root of this lower-bound scale into
\[
n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}
\]
up to universal constant factors.  Under the weakened estimator-bounded condition in Remark 2, including when the baseline response is known, the corresponding treated-side square-root lower-bound form is \(n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}\).  These are lower bounds in the source paper's estimator-bounded WATE class; the citation does not assert a matching upper bound or a minimax equivalence for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: For any constant $\gamma\in\left({1}/{2},1\right)$ and estimators $\hat{m}(x)$ and $\hat{g}(d,x)$ that satisfy Assumption \ref{asmp:estimator-bounded}, for any given weight function $w$, the minimax risk of estimating the \textsc{WATE} is $\mathfrak{M}_{n,\gamma}^{\wate}\left(\gF_{e_n,e_n',f_n}\right) = \Omega\left( \max\{e_n,e_n'\} f_n\cdot\Vert w\Vert _{P_X,\infty}^2 + \Vert w\Vert_{P_X,2}^2/n\right)$. If we only assume that $c\leq\hat{m}(x), \hat{g}(1,x) \leq 1-c$ in Assumption \ref{asmp:estimator-bounded}, then we would have the lower bound $\mathfrak{M}_{n,\gamma}^{\wate}\left(\gF_{e_n,e_n',f_n}\right) = \Omega\left( e_n' f_n\cdot\Vert w\Vert _{P_X,\infty}^2 + \Vert w\Vert_{P_X,2}^2/n\right)$. Furthermore, this lower bound still holds in the case where we know the baseline response, \emph{i.e.,} $\hat{g}(0,x)=g_0(0,x)=0$.

In the pure structure-agnostic class \(\mathcal P(\varepsilon_n,\delta_n)\) of BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, defined for two arbitrary nuisance estimates whose \(L^2\) errors are at most \(\varepsilon_n\) and \(\delta_n\), Section 2 states for its single mean functional \(\psi\) that no estimator has convergence rate faster than
\[
n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n.
\]
This cited statement is confined to that single functional and the source class \(\mathcal P(\varepsilon_n,\delta_n)\). It does not by itself establish a control-arm analogue, a joint two-arm full-ATE minimax equivalence, a two-product lower bound for one common ATE experiment, or a matching upper bound for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: Given two arbitrary estimators $\widehat\omega(x)$ and $\widehat\mu(x)$, the class $\mathcal{P}(\epsilon_n,\delta_n)$ consists of all densities such that $\lVert\widehat\omega-\omega\rVert\leq\epsilon_n$ and $\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert\leq\delta_n$. Our first result is that the rate of convergence of any estimator of $\psi$ over this class cannot be faster than $n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_n\cdot\delta_n$.
